decision: Which approach best resolves: A mutual action plan can be refused. How should the room record a refusal, given that the vendor makes APPROVER a distinct role whose rule is 'Must approve before signers can sign', while a SIGNER refuses the document terms?

state.problem: A mutual action plan can be refused. How should the room record a refusal, given that the vendor makes APPROVER a distinct role whose rule is 'Must approve before signers can sign', while a SIGNER refuses the document terms?

candidate_solutions.two_milestones: Record refused_by_approver and refused_by_signer as two separate milestones. An approver refuses before any signature is gathered, so the seller can fix the plan and send it again; a signer refuses the terms, so it does not go out unchanged. Costs one more milestone value in the served vocabulary.
candidate_solutions.one_refused: Record a single refused milestone for both. Costs no extra vocabulary and one simpler state machine, but the seller cannot tell whether to edit and resend or to abandon, and the research's one emphasised role becomes indistinguishable.
candidate_solutions.one_refused_with_flag: Record a single refused milestone and carry the refusing role as a field on the refusal. Keeps the milestone list short while preserving who refused, but a reader of the milestone alone still cannot tell the two cases apart.
candidate_solutions.no_refusal_milestone: Do not move the milestone on a refusal at all. Record the recipient's status and leave the plan awaiting signature. Rejected because a plan a buyer said no to would sit in the room looking like it was merely pending.

context.research_quote: APPROVER | Must approve before signers can sign
context.research_quote_2: A buyer can instead reject (DOCUMENT_REJECTED, rejectionReason)
context.why: The distinguishing fact is what the seller can do next. An approver's no means the plan can be corrected and re-sent; a signer's no means the terms are the problem. One badge has to drive two different next actions, so the milestone itself carries the difference.
context.cost_of_the_rejected_alternative: Collapsing the two into one refused milestone loses exactly the distinction the research's approver rule exists for, and a flag on the record does not restore it for a reader scanning the milestone list.
context.evidence: test_wf067.py asserts an approver refusal and a signer refusal land on two different milestones. test_wf067_http.py asserts the same over HTTP. Both were confirmed live over real HTTP.

per_rule_coverage.shared_file_guard: test_wf067_http.py diffs the branch against origin/main and fails if any shared file appears. git status shows only new files; no tracked file is modified.
per_rule_coverage.domain_purity: test_wf067.py reads every module of the domain package off disk and asserts it contains no sqlite3, no dsr.api, no dsr.deps, no fastapi, no AuditedDatabase(, no _conn and no db_path.

known_limits: Coverage was measured with four other agents running on the same host, so it understates the true figure. CI re-measures on an unshared runner.
No browser verification was performed: no screenshot and no rendered-page check. The page was verified by build, lint and by its API contract only.
The frontend page has no dedicated component test of its own. The 468 passing frontend tests are the pre-existing suite; this feature adds none.

No vendor sandbox was contacted. Documenso was not called over the network at any point, so the webhook contract is verified against the research's documented behaviour rather than against the live vendor.
